economics.intervention-pol-analyse-1.000.all: Plan: fines raise cost of breaking limit, incentive to comply, cap waste; permits cap total waste (cut 21%), price on pollution internalises external cost, firms with low abatement cost cut most; both reduce harm to third parties.

economics.intervention-pol-analyse-2.000.all: Plan: ban reduces demand for older high-emission vehicles (price falls, scrapped); grant lowers effective price of EVs so demand for EVs rises, price/quantity rise; supply of EVs may expand; less pollution.

economics.intervention-pol-assess-1.0005.all: Plan: permits give certain cap (20% cut), least-cost abatement, flexibility, revenue if auctioned; fines simple but may be too low, enforcement; permits complex, monitoring, cap may be too generous; judgement.

economics.intervention-pol-assess-2.0001.all: Plan: ban is direct and certain; but enforcement cost, hits low-income drivers; alternatives: grant/subsidy, fuel taxes, congestion charges, public transport; judgement.

economics.intervention-pol-define1.0003.all: Laws passed by government to ban or restrict an activity

economics.intervention-pol-define2.0003.all: Laws passed by the government (1) that ban, restrict or control an activity e.g. pollution (1)

economics.intervention-pol-diagram.0003.all: S shifts right to S1; lower price P1, higher quantity Q1

economics.intervention-pol-evaluate-1.00.all: Plan: permits certain 39% cut, efficiency, incentive to innovate; fines direct but level hard to set; permits monitoring costs, price volatility, cap level; conclusion depends on enforcement.

economics.intervention-pol-evaluate-2.00.all: Plan: ban direct, quick; enforcement, equity; grant I$2,000 may be too small; taxes/congestion charge/public transport alternatives; combined policy best; conclusion.

economics.intervention-pol-explain.0011.all: Total carbon emissions are capped (1) and fall 5% a year (1), so pollution in Eskaria is guaranteed to fall, reducing environmental damage (1)

economics.intervention-pol-mcq-auth.0003.all: C lower their price and increase quantity bought

economics.intervention-pol-mcq-class.000.all: C money given to farmers for new woodland

economics.monetary-define2.0004.all: The total amount of money (1) in circulation in an economy, e.g. notes, coins and bank deposits (1)

economics.monetary-describe.0009.all: Time lags: changes take months to affect spending, so inflation may not fall when needed (or higher rates reduce investment/growth, raise unemployment)

economics.monetary-evaluate-1.0002.all: Plan: continue - inflation still to reach target, credibility; stop - inflation falling, time lags, housing slowdown, delayed investment hurts growth, unemployment; depends on inflation vs target; conclusion.

economics.monetary-evaluate-2.0004.all: Plan: cut lowers borrowing costs, raises consumption/investment, depreciation boosts exports, inflation 0.8% leaves room; but low confidence, liquidity trap, time lags, banks may not lend; conclusion.

economics.monetary-explain.0016.all: Variable rates mean mortgage repayments rise immediately (1), reducing disposable income (1); with large mortgages the cut in spending is large (1)

economics.monetary-mcq-auth.0003.all: B the economy is in recession

economics.monetary-mcq-class.0003.all: B an appreciation of the currency

economics.monetary-mcq-def.0004.all: A the total amount of money in circulation

economics.objectives-analyse-1.0004.all: Plan: demand - classes full so excess demand, growth/profit; costs - rent, staff, finance; risk; competition in new area.

economics.objectives-analyse-2.0001.all: Plan: economies of scale lower costs; 53% share gives market power, higher prices/profit; less competition; route network expansion.

economics.objectives-analyse-3.0002.all: Plan: divorce of ownership and control; owners want profit/dividends; managers want market share, reputation, status; sustainable materials raise costs; principal-agent.

economics.objectives-assess-1.0005.all: Plan: full classes show excess demand, more revenue/economies of scale; but costs, risk, demand in new area uncertain, management stretch; judgement.

economics.objectives-assess-2.0002.all: Plan: economies of scale may lower fares, more routes; but 58% share - monopoly power, higher prices, less choice, less innovation; regulation; judgement.

economics.objectives-assess-3.0004.all: Plan: profit for owners, reinvestment; but market share, sustainability reputation may give long-run profit; costs; judgement depends on long vs short run.
